So, here is my story. I have gotten to my mid twenties, I was borderline overweight, I have been overweight before and perhaps even obese when I was in school. I have also been of a healthy weight and been underweight. However, at no point has my body actually been healthy.

I will start with my smoking, when I turned 16 I started smoking, and was smoking for 8 years or so, between 10 to 30 cigarettes a day. It was definitely an expensive addiction, costing money and health, as well as the time it takes to actually smoke (Over an hour a day wasted smoking instead of doing other stuff). However, when it came time to quit, it was actually fairly easy. I had never tried to quit before but I did it cold turkey, ignored cravings and told myself "I refuse 100% to buy cigarettes, I refuse to light them and put them near me" and that worked. It wasn't even difficult.

Now for the junk food. I wasn't a big fan of fast food restaurants but my big problem was eating mass amounts of crisps and chocolates every single day. I'd spend between £3-£10 on snacks and consume them within one day, often missing actual meals to do so. I also used to drink about 1-2litres of coke/energy drink every day. My teas and coffees would have 3 or 4 teaspoons of sugar, I also work in a food place and would be offered free hot chocolates with whipped cream every day, free melted cheese sandwiches etc. It was a fucking mess. I decided to cut ALL of that out of my diet completely. The same way I had with smoking. I refused to buy fizzy drinks/chocolates/crisps any and all junk food. When I wanted a snack I'd eat Apples, Bananas, Grapes, Nectarines, Pears, Carrots, Peas in a pod etc. For drinks I'd switched to almost 100% water, except for my teas and coffees which now have no sugar at all. (Coffees are black, teas have a trickle of semi-skimmed milk). However the cravings were HUGE. I'd stare at the snack aisles in the shops for way too long, I'd slow down and look into bakeries longingly, and saying NO to any offers of free food at work was really difficult, I'd even pick up crisps in the shop and put them back, having to mentally berate myself for it. I almost broke so many times. I am a strong willed person, I was able to shrug off smoking with impunity, but junk food dug in deep.

I did it though, I resisted temptation and I can say I'm a lot better for it. I'm at a stable healthy weight now, I feel a lot better, my insomnia has all but vanished, I am able to run further and with less complaints, I am able to exercise for over an hour without my heart telling my to stop before it explodes. I am also saving a tonne of money because although buying as much healthy food might be more expensive pound for pound than junk food, you do not need as much healthy food as junk food to make your body feel full.

I can honestly say that quitting both smoking AND junk food has benefited me greatly. It was a bitch but it was necessary. I have seen too many people who I love hurt and killed by smoking/obesity related illnesses, I have been hurt by that. I don't want to hurt the people who love me in the same way.

I didn't know where to post this, so I guess it will find a home here, even if nobody reads it, I needed to get that off my chest. Junk food IS an addiction, a fucking horrible one, the worst one I've ever kicked. If you have any questions or want any help and are too embarrassed to ask in the comments, feel free to private message me.
